articles.title: U.S. to Clamp Down On AI Chip Loophole Ahead Of Trump Meeting With Xi
articles.summary: The Trump administration on Monday announced it was tightening a loophole that has allowed Chinese tech firms to bypass U.S. restrictions on accessing the most advanced A.I. chips through third countries. articles.title: Premature Birth Taught Me the Dark Comedy of Trauma
articles.summary: What followed that day is a blurry haze. When I try to remember specifics, it plays in my mind like quick cuts in a television show: A kind resident swabbing my cervix calmly, but then returning to the triage room with a larger group of doctors, all with somber faces. A fast transfer to a labor and delivery room. A steroid shot for my baby’s lungs and a magnesium drip for his brain; IV antibiotics and a fetal monitor. Our son, holding on. articles.title: In Hakeem Jeffries’ Rise to Speaker, Black Leaders See a Milestone—and a Test
articles.summary: In 1870, Joseph Rainey of South Carolina became the first Black person to serve in the U.S. House. This week, current and newly elected House Democrats are poised to meet to select Rep. Hakeem Jeffries as the chamber’s first Black Speaker. It is a moment fraught with meaning and hurdles for both the New York Democrat and the larger Black community, multiple Black leaders tell TIME. articles.title: How to Build an Artificial Intelligence Revolution for All
articles.summary: The most important flashpoint in the debate over the future of artificial intelligence for both business and political leaders is: What is the impact of the technology on working Americans? Over the long term, AI’s promise will be measured not by the scale of its investment, disruption, or productivity, but by the apportionment across America of the value it creates.
